title: ArcCivs autonomous settlement finite stock and generic production
assumptions: Before the admin-created autonomous settlement mode is absent; after includes only autonomous settlements. Existing personal settlements are unchanged.

Low/base/high are 1/10/500 autonomous cities on one home backend under one administrator, with an assumed 0.25/1/4 hours per day for that backend's production pool. These are one-backend sensitivity assumptions, not measured sessions. participants=[1,1,1] therefore counts one admin in each case; city scaling is already in item-flow event counts. The scenarios do not aggregate or multiply across other home backends.

All assessed cities use the completed level-2 profile. Each city has two worker slots at each of Forester, Quarry and Farm, for six producers; level-2 delivery is 8 wood or 6 stone/food per completed producer trip. Level 1 is 4/3/3.

The low case has two active producer workers per resource for 15 minutes (30 deliveries/resource/day). Base/high assume this home backend's 48 active-NPC cap is fully allocated to production, evenly split as 16 producers/resource; for 60/240 minutes this is 960/3840 deliveries/resource/day. Personal-settlement NPC use on the same home backend reduces autonomous headroom; other backends have separate limits. The 48 limit is per-home-backend concurrency, not a measured per-day total.

Delivery quantities are gross, theoretical upper bounds at one completed delivery per worker per 60 seconds. The autonomous branch requires real storage arrival; path/travel, night shelter, hunger work slowdown, unavailable chunks/depot, and the 640-per-resource stock capacity reduce or stop realized deliveries. Item flows are not net stock accumulation.

Each new autonomous city receives one-time abstract non-transferable stock: 96 wood, 96 stone, 24 food. This lifecycle amount is listed separately because the evaluator models recurring per-player-day events.

Construction reserves and consumes the exact finite stock cost once per building/upgrade. Costs and full-profile totals are included separately; no construction cadence is assumed as a daily burn. Five initial immigrant admissions are a separate free budget; later recruitment costs 12 food, at most one resident per two active minutes, subject to room and food.
Food stock can be consumed for hunger: one food restores six hunger. Resident hunger/recruitment cadence and city occupancy are conditional, so food sinks are not fabricated as daily event counts.

Physical city stock has capacity 128 plus the active Warehouse level addition; the completed level-2 profile therefore holds at most 640 of each resource per city. This is an inventory ceiling, not a lifetime or weekly cap.

No Vault, premium-token or Minecraft player-XP flow is added. Abstract village stock is not a player item grant or a currency proxy. Real schematic blocks are placed by the builder; privileged admins can alter/mine their own build, while ordinary players receive no repeatable free item grant through this feature.
No item-to-currency conversion or price change is assumed. Current item SELL behavior and the planned SELL-to-contract transition remain separate, unchanged scenarios; prices are intentionally empty.

The 168-hour ledger observation is network-wide background and cannot be attributed to ArcCivs or these autonomous settlements; see the sanitized observation file. Currency totals remain separate and mixed legacy totals are not used.

Generic resource production is committed by CivsService.deliver only after real storage arrival; the separate one-minute population activeMinute path covers resident hunger/recruitment and is not counted as a passive stock-production tick.

lifetime_per_city.note: Town Hall level 1 is captured as the founding site and then constructed; its 32/24/4 cost is included. CivsRules.cost applies targetLevel squared, so the level-2 target cost is four times the level-1 base, not merely the incremental difference.

home_backend_constraints.high_500_city_sensitivity_note: 500 city slots is the configured ceiling per home backend. The one-backend 500-autonomous-city sensitivity assumes no additional personal city on that same backend. With one personal settlement on the same backend, at most 499 autonomous cities fit there; settlements on other backends use separate capacity.

unmodeled_conditional_flows.known: per-city exact lifecycle total is 840 wood, 500 stone, 28 food through the level-2 profile; timing and settlement distribution are not daily event counts.
1 food restores 6 hunger; later resident recruitment costs 12 food and is limited to one per 2 active minutes, subject to beds/population and food.
640 of each resource per completed level-2 city at a time; production pauses at capacity, while construction/hunger/recruitment consume stock.
privileged admin can alter or mine own placed schematics; no ordinary-player item grant or safe item-to-currency conversion is inferred.

source_contracts.fact: Abstract stock is non-transferable; profile, target-level costs and 96/96/24 opening stock.
Fixed cost formulas, 128+warehouse capacity and population level cap.
Building slots, resource-producing buildings, amounts per level and 60-second production interval.
Autonomous delivery requires storage arrival before CivsRules.deliver adds resource to stock.
Construction reserves fixed stock cost once; retries do not charge it again.
Backend-local configured ceilings are 500 total settlements and 48 active NPCs.
The backend-local active NPC spawn budget is bounded by that backend configuration, itself at most 48.
The default active NPC cap is a server-local limit; maximum-settlements remains a one-server ceiling.
maximum-settlements is per home backend, not network-wide.
Founding checks the home backend's existing plus pending city total against configured maximumCities.
The separate population activeMinute clock advances hunger and recruitment; it is not generic production.
Autonomous cities staff the builder and three essential producers first; level-2 auto-assignment fills a second producer slot for each resource, then the second builder slot.
A worker with hunger at or below 6 gets a doubled work interval.
Workers shelter at night outside the delivery/pickup phases.
Tests confirm the four essential jobs, six producer workers at level 2, and a simulated full profile sustained by autonomous stock deliveries.
